- The multiplier: Gartner's 2026 analysis puts agentic AI at 5-30x the tokens per task of a chatbot exchange.
- The cause: every tool call re-sends the full context; a TechAhead fraud-check agent used ~13,500 tokens across 5 steps against ~800 for one chat turn (2026).
- The variance: Stanford's Digital Economy Lab saw identical SWE-bench agent runs differ by up to 30x in token cost (2026).
- The billing fix: a rented GPU bills by the hour, not the token; Spheron H100 runs $2.98/hr on-demand as of 14 Nov 2026.
- The biggest lever: prefix and KV caching of the repeated context. See prefix caching explained.

...

On the Spheron marketplace, H100 on-demand rentals start from $2.98/hr per GPU, and spot instances from $2.20/hr per GPU, as of 14 Nov 2026 (Spheron GPU offers API). Spot capacity can be reclaimed without notice, so plan for restarts if you run executors on it. Run an 8B-14B executor model on that hardware for agent tool-calling steps, and your cost per agent-hour is fixed regardless of whether that hour produces 10 tool calls or 40. Compare that to the fintech case above: $5,000 a month at 50 users works out to roughly $100 per user, and $15,000 a month at 500 users works out to roughly $30 per user, a lower per-user rate that still adds up to 3x the total bill, because concurrency-driven retries and longer contexts push total token volume up faster than user count. A dedicated GPU running the same workload has a cost ceiling set by the hardware rental rate, not by how badly a given day's agent trajectories snowball.

> Pricing fluctuates based on GPU availability. Spheron rates above are live as of 14 Nov 2026; other providers reflect their most recent published rates and may have changed. Check current GPU pricing → for live rates.

The break-even math depends on volume and how token-hungry your agent architecture actually is, not just on the sticker price of tokens. Our AI inference cost economics playbook works through the general cost-per-token math for self-hosted inference; the agent case just pushes token volume high enough, and makes it variable enough, that the crossover to self-hosted GPU-hour billing arrives sooner than it would for a chat product at the same user count. results.title: FLUX 3 GPU Requirements: Video, Audio & Image Setup (2026) | Spheron Blog
results.author: Mitrasish ,  Co-founder & CTO, Spheron
highlights:
- Official answer: Black Forest Labs has published no parameter count or VRAM figure for any FLUX 3 variant as of 3 Aug 2026; Video and Action are API-only early access.
- Planning proxy: FLUX.2-dev (32B) needs ~64GB at BF16, ~32GB at FP8 and ~19GB at GGUF Q4_K_S, so budget an 80GB-class GPU for FLUX 3 Dev.
- Only published number: FLUX-mimic runs robot-action inference in under 80ms on one RTX 5090 (Jul 2026).
- Run today: FLUX.2 at FP8 on an H100 or A100 80G; Spheron A100 runs $1.48/hr on-demand as of 14 Nov 2026.
- Quantized tier: FLUX.2 GGUF Q4_K_S fits a 24GB RTX 4090. Compare live GPU pricing.

...

It's an application process, not a purchase: you describe your use case and wait for BFL to approve or hold the request, with no published wait times or acceptance criteria. Pricing hasn't been published either, so any per-generation cost you see quoted before BFL ships an official pricing page is a guess, not a fact.

| Variant | Quantization | VRAM | Minimum GPU |

| FLUX.2 Dev | BF16 | ~64GB | Needs >80GB; use FP8 instead |
| FLUX.2 Dev | FP8 | ~32GB | H100 or A100 80G |
| FLUX.2 Dev | GGUF Q8_0 | ~35GB | H100 or A100 80G |
| FLUX.2 Dev | GGUF Q4_K_S | ~19GB | RTX 4090 |
| FLUX.2-klein-4B | FP8/BF16 | ~13GB | RTX 4090 and above |

If FLUX 3 Dev follows a similar quantization curve, an H100 covers FP8 inference comfortably, and A100 SXM4 80G spot is the value play for batch or checkpointable workloads. Neither is a guarantee, since FLUX 3's actual parameter count is still unknown, but it's the same reasoning that has worked for every prior FLUX release.
